Into the Woods.notes: Recorded on an external audio recorder. The venue was a church so there's a lot of echoing. The recorder picked up some of the actor's voices as well as the speakers so the dialogue especially sounds a bit off. Some mics were off, especially Cinderella's Stepmother's. Audience was wild; full of families and friends of the performers. The Princes were so committed to not walking period and it was hysterical. High-kicks and Maria heel clicks the entire time.Includes digital program.

Legally Blonde.cast: Paul Canaan, Natalie Joy Johnson, Leslie Rodriguez Kritzer
Legally Blonde.notes: MY NOTES: A joint opening night gift from Laurence O'Keefe, Nell Benjamin, Paul Canaan, and Gaelen Gilliand to the rest cast. Includes two songs, the first being "The Bonecake Remix" which splices together some cut lines and inside jokes from the cast set to what Christian Borle once called a "phat beat." The second is "One at a Time," a song written by Larry and Nell sung by Paul. Natalie Joy Johnson and Leslie Rodriguez Kritzer sing backup. I honestly have no clue what the context is and am not sure I want to know.

Legally Blonde.notes: MY NOTES: A promo version of the OBCR which was sent out to Tony Voters before the official release. In addition to including the overture, it has an extended "What You Want" dance sequence, encore music for "There! Right There!", and some lead in dialogue for "Bend and Snap". The hidden "Kyle the Magnificent" track in Find My Way was cut and placed into its proper place in the album.

The Music Man.notes: A lovely performance of this lovely revival of THE MUSIC MAN, even with the awful lyric changes to “Shipoopi” - if you’re going to sanitize it, you still have to be clever! That said, Kathy is a lovely, lovely Marian who sings the songs beautifully in the keys as written, which is such a treat. Jayne Houdyshell left no scenery unchewed. This is the kind of role Hugh Jackman is perfect for (deception? By someone who hangs with the Trumps? Never!), and he is pretty stellar, in my humble opinion.
